title: Mixed tensor-action squares transfer to counit-defined projection mates
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], each with a specified bifunctor denoted $\otimes$. Give functors $P_r:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$, $P_p:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ with adjunctions $P_r\dashv R_r$, $P_p\dashv R_p$, units $\eta_r,\eta_p$ and counits $\varepsilon_r,\varepsilon_p$; give functors $P_i:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, $P_k:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $K:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, and a specified natural identification $P_rP_i\cong P_kP_p$. Supply natural tensor comparisons $\mu_h:P_h(U\otimes V)\to P_hU\otimes P_hV$ for $h=r,p$, and natural mixed action comparisons
$$d_i(H,N):JH\otimes N\to J(H\otimes P_iN),\qquad d_k(M,V):KM\otimes V\to K(M\otimes P_kV).$$
Let $a:P_pJ\to KP_r$ be a natural transformation satisfying, for every $H\in\mathcal C$, $N\in\mathcal D$,
$$K(\mu_r)a_{H\otimes P_iN}P_p(d_i)=d_k(a_H\otimes1_{P_pN})\mu_p,$$
under the specified identification. No monoidal structure on $J,K$ is assumed: $d_i,d_k$ have the mixed domains displayed above. Define $g:JR_r\to R_pK$ to be the proper-adjunction mate of $a$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], namely $g=R_p(K\varepsilon_r)R_p(aR_r)\eta_pJR_r$. For $h=r,p$ define $\pi_{h;M,Q}:R_hM\otimes Q\to R_h(M\otimes P_hQ)$ as the $P_h\dashv R_h$-transpose of $(\varepsilon_{h,M}\otimes1)\mu_h$.
For every $M\in\mathcal A$, $N\in\mathcal D$, put $E=R_rM$, $X=P_iN$, $T=P_rX=P_kP_pN$, $Z=M\otimes T$, and $c=(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1_T)\mu_r:P_r(E\otimes X)\to Z$. The two maps
$$g_ZJ(\pi_{r;M,X})d_i(E,N),\qquad R_p(d_k(M,P_pN))\pi_{p;KM,N}(g_M\otimes1_N)$$
from $JE\otimes N$ to $R_pKZ$ have the same $P_p\dashv R_p$-transpose, precisely
$$K(c)a_{E\otimes X}P_p(d_i(E,N)):P_p(JE\otimes N)\longrightarrow KZ.$$
In particular the two maps are equal, naturally in $M,N$. The assertion requires neither invertibility of $a,g,\pi_h,\mu_h,d_i,d_k$ nor any exactness, boundedness or Tor hypothesis. For unbounded ringed-site categories the counit-defined maps of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] are these $\pi_h$.

proof.text: Write composition right to left and suppress only the specified natural identification $P_rP_i\cong P_kP_p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], the inverse adjunction bijection sends $b:U\to R_hV$ to $\tau_h(b)=\varepsilon_{h,V}P_h(b)$. Its naturality gives $\tau_h(R_h(v)bu)=v\tau_h(b)P_h(u)$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], $\tau_p(g_V)=K(\varepsilon_{r,V})a_{R_rV}$. By the stipulated definition of $\pi_h$, $\tau_h(\pi_{h;V,Q})=(\varepsilon_{h,V}\otimes1_{P_hQ})\mu_{h;R_hV,Q}$. These identities use only the given adjunctions, not any invertibility.

proof.text:
Put $\pi_r=\pi_{r;M,X}$ and $d_i=d_i(E,N)$. The transpose of the first map is
$$\tau_p(g_ZJ(\pi_r)d_i)=K(\varepsilon_{r,Z})a_{R_rZ}P_pJ(\pi_r)P_p(d_i)=K(\varepsilon_{r,Z})K P_r(\pi_r)a_{E\otimes X}P_p(d_i).$$
The first equality is the mate transpose of Step 1 with precomposition; the second is naturality of $a$ at $\pi_r:E\otimes X\to R_rZ$. The defining transpose of $\pi_r$ says $\varepsilon_{r,Z}P_r(\pi_r)=c$. Functoriality of $K$ therefore makes this transpose exactly $K(c)a_{E\otimes X}P_p(d_i)$.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; agent mixed tensor-action mate calculation, returned lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate steps 4–6 (not a theorem quoted verbatim from Stacks).

proof.text:
Abbreviate $V=P_pN$, $d_k=d_k(M,V)$ and $\mu_p=\mu_{p;JE,N}$. Taking the transpose of the second map, using [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] and the defining transpose of $\pi_p$, gives
$$\tau_p\bigl(R_p(d_k)\pi_{p;KM,N}(g_M\otimes1_N)\bigr)=d_k(\varepsilon_{p,KM}\otimes1_V)\mu_{p;R_pKM,N}P_p(g_M\otimes1_N).$$
Naturality of $\mu_p$ in its first variable rewrites this as $d_k((\varepsilon_{p,KM}P_p(g_M))\otimes1_V)\mu_p$. The mate identity [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] at $M$ then rewrites it as
$$d_k\bigl((K(\varepsilon_{r,M})a_E)\otimes1_V\bigr)\mu_p.$$

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; agent mixed tensor-action mate calculation, returned lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate steps 4–6 (not a theorem quoted verbatim from Stacks).

proof.text:
Naturality of the mixed comparison $d_k$ in its first variable, at $\varepsilon_{r,M}:P_rE\to M$, is precisely
$$d_k(M,V)(K(\varepsilon_{r,M})\otimes1_V)=K(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1_{P_kV})d_k(P_rE,V).$$
Substitute this in Step 3 and use bifunctoriality of $\otimes$ to separate $K(\varepsilon_{r,M})a_E$. The resulting expression is
$$K(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1_T)d_k(P_rE,V)(a_E\otimes1_V)\mu_p.$$
The hypothesized mixed tensor square at $H=E,N=N$ replaces its last three factors by $K(\mu_{r;E,X})a_{E\otimes X}P_p(d_i(E,N))$. Since $c=(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1_T)\mu_{r;E,X}$, functoriality of $K$ identifies the expression with $K(c)a_{E\otimes X}P_p(d_i(E,N))$. This proves the specified common-transpose formula.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; agent mixed tensor-action mate calculation, returned lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate steps 4–6 (not a theorem quoted verbatim from Stacks).

proof.text:
The inverse hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] is injective. The two maps therefore agree by Steps 2 and 4. For completeness, the projection families used here are natural: if $m:M\to M'$ and $q:Q\to Q'$, naturality of the counit and $\mu_h$ gives, writing $c_h(M,Q)=(\varepsilon_{h,M}\otimes1)\mu_{h;R_hM,Q}$,
$$c_h(M',Q')P_h(R_h(m)\otimes q)=(m\otimes P_h(q))c_h(M,Q).$$
Indeed insert naturality of $\mu_h$, then $m\varepsilon_{h,M}=\varepsilon_{h,M'}P_hR_h(m)$, and combine the two tensor factors by bifunctoriality. Naturality of the adjunction bijection transposes this equality to naturality of $\pi_h$. The mate $g$ is natural by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; all other comparisons are natural by hypothesis. Thus the equality is natural in $M,N$.

proof.text: For the unbounded ringed-site interpretation, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] specifies the natural transformation adjoint to $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\mu_{RE,P}$. This is exactly the defining transpose of the present $\pi_{h;E,P}$, so uniqueness in the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] identifies the two maps. The cited statement permits arbitrary unbounded objects. Steps 1–5 only used naturality, bifunctoriality, adjunction bijections and the supplied mixed square. They neither invert any comparison nor use exactness, bounds or Tor amplitude, proving all the asserted scope clauses.
